title.narrative: Catchment to Tap (C2T)

description.narrative: The proposed Catchment to Tap (C2T) programme has the goal of improving access and availability of clean and safe water in adequate quantities and sanitation services for all users, as well as enhance climate resilience and inclusivity in the water sector. The programme will be implemented around the Rift Valley Basin. The programme will also have a light-touch in the Upper Tana Basin (Thika catchment) and Lake Victoria South Basin (Homa Bay), where the partners are able to leverage existing work through the WaterWorX and Blue Deal projects. The project’s activities will be implemented through an integrated approach centred around the IWRMWASH nexus demonstrations in Module 2. Through participatory approaches with the communities, particularly women and youth, the project will implement IWRM-WASH nexus demonstrations using a catchment approach, taking into account the human and climate induced changes degrading water source areas and impacting downstream users’ water supply and health outcomes. The catchment approach also facilitates the identification of bankable projects and the team will support additional high potential interventions with technical expertise to demonstrate sustainable business models that can be invested in and scaled through external finance. While each module will achieve specific outcomes, Module 1, 3 and 4 will create the necessary enabling conditions for the demonstration projects in Module 2 - i.e. raise awareness on the importance of IWRMWASH, increase capacity and knowledge in IWRM institutions, and improve institutional systems and structures with the WRA (Nakuru, Kisumu, and Embu) and WRUAs. Each module’s design builds sustainability and ownership of IWRM-WASH through IWRM institutions.

recipient-country.narrative: Kenya is the recipient country, through WWF Kenya -some resources go to 3 Dutch organizations (World Water Net, Vei and Acacia Water)

sector.narrative: Water is a finite natural resource and a key driver of economic and social development. Optimal sustainable management of water resources requires conducive enabling environment, a coordinated multi stakeholder and multi-sectoral approach. In 2023, the project continued to align with key national and county government strategies, strengthening the enabling environment; efforts geared towards C2T desired ultimate goal of enhancing water security in Kenya. The project within this reporting period, emphasised sustainable and holistic water resource management through sustained awareness creation and calling for action, rolled out strategic interventions through demonstrations of best practices, engagement with key stakeholders and building coalitions of right holders, and using evidence based advocacy to lobby decision makers or duty bearers on the need to prioritise Water Resources Management (WRM) for sustainable Water Access and Hygiene (WASH) investments. A significant financing gap exists for achieving SDG 6, both globally and in Kenya, making it challenging to meet 2030 targets. Transformational changes are needed in the water resources and WASH sectors to bridge this gap. In that regard, the Privatisation Act 2023 was assented to in October 2023. The law provides the legal framework for private sector to support and bridge the Ksh.500 billion funding deficit towards the envisioned universal access to water and sanitation. However, the Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) are concerned that the private sector's high appetite for return on investments and the clamour for high water levies may discredit the need to uphold the constitutionally recognised- fundamental human right on access to water and sanitation services, especially for the majority of the low income vulnerable community members. As a matter of great public interest, the CSOs developed a position paper to highlight the risks and at the same time advocate for safeguards and a solution ‘‘value-chain’ approach to guide a more sustainable water future for Kenya. The proposed water sector amendment laws i.e. Water Act amendment bill (2023), Water regulation 2023, Water harvesting and storage regulation 2023 and Water Sector Trust Fund Regulations 2023 provide good opportunity for C2T project to engage for purposes of strengthening IWRM as these are bound to significantly influence water management in Kenya going forward. The project took cognisance of the opportunities through advocacy and strategic engagements to draw attention to the amendments and will continue to convene sessions with other key stakeholders to ensure enabling environment for effective implementation of IWRM. In addition, the Ministry of Water, Sanitation and Irrigation (MoWSI)and Council of Governors (CoG) signed the intergovernmental framework on water resources management. As part of aforementioned opportunities, efforts are underway including a position paper developed with recommendations to advocate for establishment of Basin Water Resources Committees (BWRCs) to strengthen collaboration within the sector. Kenya signed up to the Freshwater Challenge in 2023, and joined the list of 20 Countries in Africa and 43 globally who have committed to restore 300,000 Km of riparian and 350 M Ha of wetlands. This country led ambition aligns perfectly with the C2T’s ambition of collective action towards restoration of critical water resources and efforts are underway to support the country to make a step further and set national targets, align appropriately with climate change frameworks and be ready to benefit from global climate finance facilities.

policy-marker.narrative: The DAC gender equality policy marker is based on a three-point scoring system, to qualitatively track the financial flows that target gender equality. This allows the OECD to identify gaps between DAC donors’ policy commitments and financial commitments. The marker strengthens the transparency and accountability in development financing for gender equality and women’s rights. At present, 92% of total bilateral “sector-allocable” aid is screened against the gender equality marker. • Principal (marked 2) means that gender equality is the main objective of the project/programme and is fundamental is its design and expected results. The project/programme would not have been undertaken without this objective. • Significant (marked 1) means that gender equality is an important and deliberate objective, but not the principal reason for undertaking the project/programme, often explained as gender equality being mainstreamed in the project/programme. • Not targeted (marked 0) means that the project/programme has been screened against the gender marker but has not been found to target gender equality.

title.narrative: The output results areas are in 3 components: Component 1: Awareness. Lobby and advocacy ‘Awareness on when to act and how’ Component 2: Knowledge sharing and capacity development ‘Key actors being able to act and improve’ Component 3: Improved systems and structures ‘A better performing WRM sector’

description.narrative:
1. Enhanced Public Sensitization on IWRM; Estimated 1.5M people were reached through thought leadership Op-ed articles through various media channels, promoted IWRM and mobilized the public including organized school children competitions based on project aligned essays, amplifying the call to strengthen IWRM in Kenya. Additional estimated 4 million Kenyans reached through ‘Journey of River Malewa’ public campaign walking from the source of the river to the mouth (approx. 18.8 km) highlighting increasing water and related climate risks in Kenya in general and specifically in Lake Naivasha basin with notable post on IWRM positive actions from the stakeholders.
2. Improved Advocacy and Communication Skills: Established a Citizen-led River Health Assessment (RHA) in Njoro sub-catchment, and the WRUA empowered to articulate water related concerns and supporting pertinent field data acquisition while taking responsibility in strengthening water resources management in the basin. Notable issues that were raised include pollution cases that were reported to WRA and led follow up on compliance to effluent discharge regulations. The RHA will also be used as an advocacy tool for holding the duty bearers to account on IWRM related functions.
3. Strengthened platforms for IWRM for WASH Practitioners; Out of 44 (34M: 10 F) representatives of WASH practitioners, 10 committed to lobby for inclusion in catchment management initiatives in respective organizations strategic or investment plans. The commitments were captured in the assessment report and will be followed up in year 3. IWRM Policy related gaps identified in collaboration with the Ministry of Water, Sanitation and Irrigation, and other stakeholders as a basis for informed strategic engagements aimed at transforming water resources management in the country. 4. Developed Knowledge Development Plan; the plan incorporates seven (7) IWRM pertinent modules used as the basis for training-enhancing key stakeholders’ skills and capacity on IWRM for WASH in Kenya, including the need to strengthen climate change adaptation/mitigation and mainstreaming of gender in IWRM approaches, plans and implementation.
5. Enhanced Capacity of IWRM authorities/institutions; Eighty-Seven 87 (31F:56M) WRA staff trained based on previously identified knowledge gaps, strengthening the agency to ensure effective execution of its mandate as a regulator. The trainings entailed Climate Change and Gender Integration aspects.
6. Developed Demonstrations1 Intake Form for stakeholders to take action on IWRM; the draft demonstrations intake forms will enable stakeholder led strengthening of IWRM cases in Kenya. The intake form is deliberate in identifying IWRM solutions that will also address climate change and promote gender equity.

title.narrative: Number of actions taken to resolve water issues in meeting future water demands as a result advocacy campaigns

description.narrative: There are 6 actions taken by key actors in the water sector within this reporting period to resolve water issues and work towards increasing water access for now and for the future. ● County governments in Ewaso Nyiro North basin are implementing commitments made during the 2nd edition of the ‘journey of water’. On one hand, Isiolo County developed the Isiolo County Water Strategy that seeks to increase access to clean and safe drinking water for people, livestock and wildlife and promote sustainable management of water resources. On the other hand, Laikipia County has led clean-up activities and invested in restoration of riparian land to reduce pollution in R. Nanyuki, a tributary of R. Ewaso North. ● The WRUA’s are also raising awareness on water pollution, impacts of climate change such as droughts and floods through evidence based advocacy by participating in media talk shows on both mainstream and social media. They have been part of over 30 news features. ● Youths under the umbrella of ‘Kenya Water Ambassadors’ have taken lead in amplifying voices - calling for collective action on water resources through mainstream and social media campaigns, and conducted 3 mini journeys of water under the hashtag #Voices4rivers, #JourneyofWater under the following handles Kenya Water Ambassadors @KenyaWaterAmb and taking responsibility-undertaking rivers clean-up activities (#youths4change) to reduce water pollution. ● Strengthened IWRM forum under the department of water resources, min. of water, sanitation and irrigation. The forum is used to aggregate and validate information on SDG 6.5.1. on the degree of implementation of integrated Water Resource Management (IWRM) in the country. ● Faith Based Organisations (FBOs) formed a forum-formed an association and elected leaders in readiness to champion WRM-WASH nexus in their respective localities, although they are not formally registered, the group is actively involved in advocacy on responsible sand harvesting in Makueni. ● Through C2T efforts, the Kenya government joined the rest of the global community in the Freshwater challenge-a global pledge to restore 300,000Km of rivers and 350M ha of wetlands as part of the countries efforts to tackle climate change and manage water risks. The project will support the MoWSI and Laikipia County to develop country targets to operationalize the commitments.

description.narrative: This indicator will track the number of people /WRM stakeholders trained IWRM -WASH topics. The trainings will be on technical and strategic topics such as climate resilience, IT skills, GIS, data collection, applied data handling, digital data devices and analytics, IWRM-WASH C2T skills, mandates towards BWRCs, advocacy, communication, conflict management, human-rights based approaches, gender mainstreaming, and working harmoniously with county leadership, and applied C2T approaches. Stakeholders will include WRA staff from regional and sub-regional offices, WRUA members, and other organizations involved in IWRM for WaSH within the project area. The trainings will be both general for WRM stakeholders, as well as targeted technical trainings for each stakeholder based on the stakeholder's mandate, e.g specific trainings for WRUAs. This indicator captures training activities across all project outcomes
